newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast refined products steady after APIs.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast refined products steady after APIs.

text.p: Prices for U.S. West Coast products were notionally steady Wednesday, with energy futures failing to give direction and gasoline supplies stable, traders said.

June crude oil on New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX) shaded 11 cents a barrel higher to $19.70 a barrel around 12:15 p.m. PDT (1915 GMT), as futures traders reacted to excess prompt supply and saw unleaded futures weighing crude.
May gasoline, which expires April 30, fell 0.17 cents a gallon to 61.60 cents a gallon.
April/May prices for ultra-clean CARB gasoline were unchanged at 70/71 cents a gallon, while San Francisco CARB was pegged one cent less.
Conventional unleaded gasoline for prompt delivery stood 65/66 cents, with San Francisco at the same price.
Distillates were also flat Wednesday, with heating oil up a moderate 0.77 cents gallon.

Traders also yawned at the American Petroleum Institute's report late Tuesday of a 578,000-barrel-build in West Coast gasoline stocks that left inventories in the PADD 5 region at 26.7 million last week.
